# Engine: each reviewer's own instructions, repo file and `files` filter in its prompt

## What to build

Already in the codebase (from an earlier slice): `packages/graph-execution/src/review/reviewers.ts` with `reviewerSchema` / `type Reviewer` (`{ id, type: "diff"|"tester", name, enabled, instructions, repoFile, provider?, model?, files?, blockAt }`), `BUILTIN_REVIEWERS` (`code`: `repoFile: "REVIEW.md"`, `tester`: `repoFile: "TESTING.md"`), `BUILTIN_INSTRUCTIONS` (exactly the first two lines of today's code reviewer and tester prompts), `matchFiles(files, globs)`, `stepName`, `notPerformed`, `reviewerAgent`. `runReviewPhase` takes `reviewers?: readonly Reviewer[]` and `reviewRound` runs every reviewer: `type: "diff"` through `runCodeReviewer({ ...shared, kind: reviewer.id, name: reviewer.name, ... })`, `type: "tester"` through `runLiveTester`. Today every diff reviewer still gets the code reviewer's fixed prompt and every reviewer gets the fixed `REVIEW.md`/`TESTING.md`.

This slice makes each reviewer's prompt its own, as the spec asks (`docs/prd/ui-reviewers.md`, "Engine: review round", decisions on instructions and repo files; KAN-87):
- **Two layers per reviewer**: its general `instructions` (from the reviewers file / the UI) replace the fixed role text at the top of the prompt, and its own `repoFile`, read from the **repo root** (uncommitted is fine), adds that repo's rules. A reviewer gets **only its own** repo file, never another reviewer's. A missing file is not an error: the reviewer works from its instructions and, at round 0, the run logs `no <file> at the repo root` (built-ins keep today's exact lines).
- **`files` globs** limit a diff reviewer's diff to the matching changed files; no match → a "not needed" report without running the agent.
- The **tester** keeps its runner; its `instructions` replace the role text of `testerPrompt` and its `repoFile` takes the place of `TESTING.md`.
- The engine keeps the fixed frame: report path, JSON shape, finding rules, previous-round verification, human comment verdicts.
- **Byte-for-byte**: with `BUILTIN_REVIEWERS`, the code reviewer's and tester's prompts must be identical to today's (existing inline snapshots in `agents/tester.test.ts` and prompt assertions in `review/phase-*.test.ts` must pass unchanged).
- A test hook for out-of-process checks: when `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_PROMPTS=<dir>` is set, the fake provider writes every prompt to `<dir>/<role>-<label>.md` (e.g. `reviewer-security-r0.md`, `fixer-fix-r1.md`). The detached `--web` launcher already forwards every `GRAPH_EXECUTION_*` env var (`launch/script.ts:43-44`).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/context.ts` (whole file, 86 lines) — `REVIEW_FILE`/`TESTING_FILE` (lines 7-8), `ReviewerContextOptions`, `ReviewerContext` (`reviewMd`, `testingMd`), `buildReviewerContext` reads both files with `readOptional`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/context.test.ts` (61 lines) — asserts `ctx.reviewMd`/`ctx.testingMd` and `not.toHaveProperty("reviewMd")`; must keep passing.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/reviewer.ts` lines 69-177 `codeReviewerPrompt(ctx, round, reportPath, previous?, comments = [])`:
  - 76-79 the two role lines (= `BUILTIN_INSTRUCTIONS.code`);
  - 93-95 `if (ctx.reviewMd !== undefined) out.push("## Review rules (REVIEW.md)", "", ctx.reviewMd.trimEnd(), "");`
  - 96-99 the first Instructions bullet `"- Review the diff for bugs, security problems and correctness against the specification" + (ctx.reviewMd !== undefined ? ", and for violations of the review rules above." : ".")`;
  - 145-176 the example report with `reviewer: "code"` and the line `` `It must be a JSON object of this shape, with \`round\` ${round} and \`reviewer\` "code"; …` ``.
  - lines 414-422 `runCodeReviewer` (already takes `kind`/`name`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/tester.ts` lines 47-171 `testerPrompt(ctx, round, reportPath, previous?)`:
  - 48-50 role lines (= `BUILTIN_INSTRUCTIONS.tester`);
  - 66-68 `out.push("## How to test this app (TESTING.md)", "", ctx.testingMd.trimEnd(), "")`;
  - 82-85 `"- Follow TESTING.md above: …"` / `"- There is no TESTING.md: work out how to boot the app …"`;
  - 173-182 `runLiveTester`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/tester.test.ts` — inline snapshot of the whole tester prompt (must stay byte-identical).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase.ts` — `reviewRound` (the `buildReviewerContext({...})` call, the two `round === 0` log lines for `REVIEW.md` / `TESTING.md`, `runOne(reviewer)`, the `CODE_REVIEW_NOT_NEEDED` shortcut for `opts.reviewFiles?.length === 0`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase-live-tester.test.ts` lines 60-90 — prompt assertions (`Follow TESTING.md`, `There is no TESTING.md`, `not.toContain("(TESTING.md)")`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.ts` lines 155-175 (`run(opts)`: `calls.push(opts)`, `key`, the `FAKE_LOG_ENV` append) — add the prompt dump next to the log append; env constants at lines 10-14.
- `TESTING.md` "Fake provider scripts" — document the new env var there in one line.

## Patterns to follow

**Optional file reads** (context.ts:46-54): `readOptional(file)` returns undefined only on ENOENT.

**Prompt building**: arrays of lines joined with `\n`, `fence(text)` for embedded text, `reportPathLine(path)` for the report path (the fake provider parses it back).

**Env-driven test hooks** in the fake provider:
```ts
// providers/fake.ts:13-14, 162-163
export const FAKE_LOG_ENV = "GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_LOG";
const logFile = process.env[FAKE_LOG_ENV];
if (logFile) appendFileSync(logFile, `${key}\n`);
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/review/context.ts`

- `ReviewerContextOptions`: add `/** Repo-root files to read (each reviewer's \`repoFile\`); default \`[REVIEW_FILE, TESTING_FILE]\`. */ repoFiles?: readonly string[];`
- `ReviewerContext`: add `/** Text of each requested repo-root file that exists, by file name. */ repoFiles: Record<string, string>;`. Keep `reviewMd`/`testingMd`, set from `repoFiles["REVIEW.md"]` / `repoFiles["TESTING.md"]` when those are present (unchanged behaviour for `context.test.ts`).
- `buildReviewerContext`: read every name of `opts.repoFiles ?? [REVIEW_FILE, TESTING_FILE]` (deduplicated) with `readOptional(path.join(opts.repoRoot, name))` in the same `Promise.all`.
- Export `export function repoText(ctx: Pick<ReviewerContext, "repoFiles" | "reviewMd" | "testingMd">, file: string): string | undefined` → `ctx.repoFiles?.[file] ?? (file === REVIEW_FILE ? ctx.reviewMd : file === TESTING_FILE ? ctx.testingMd : undefined)` (the fallback serves tests that build a `ReviewerContext` by hand). Make `repoFiles` optional in the type if hand-built contexts in existing tests would otherwise fail to compile (`repoFiles?: Record<string,string>`), and always set it in `buildReviewerContext`.
- Export `export async function diffOf(integrationWorktree: string, startingCommit: string, files: readonly string[]): Promise<string>` → `git diff <start>..HEAD -- <files>` in the worktree (`""` for an empty list), using the same `execa` pattern as `buildReviewerContext`.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/reviewer.ts`

- Add a parameter object at the END of `codeReviewerPrompt` so existing callers compile: `codeReviewerPrompt(ctx, round, reportPath, previous?, comments = [], reviewer: PromptReviewer = BUILTIN_CODE)`, where
  ```ts
  export interface PromptReviewer { id: string; name: string; instructions: string; repoFile: string }
  const BUILTIN_CODE: PromptReviewer = BUILTIN_REVIEWERS[0]!; // id "code"
  ```
- Changes inside, keeping the default output byte-identical:
  - First lines: `...(reviewer.instructions.trim() === "" ? BUILTIN_INSTRUCTIONS.code : reviewer.instructions.trimEnd()).split("\n")` instead of the two literal role lines. (For a non-code reviewer with empty instructions use `` `You are the ${reviewer.name} reviewer of a change set built by AI coding agents from the specification below.` ``.)
  - Rules section: `const rules = repoText(ctx, reviewer.repoFile);` → `out.push(\`## Review rules (${reviewer.repoFile})\`, "", rules.trimEnd(), "")` when defined. (Gives `## Review rules (REVIEW.md)` for the built-in; `## Review rules (SECURITY_REVIEW.md)` for a security reviewer — the section is titled with the file name.)
  - First Instructions bullet: for `reviewer.id === "code"` exactly today's text (with `rules !== undefined` in place of `ctx.reviewMd !== undefined`). For any other id: `"- Review the diff as your instructions above ask" + (rules !== undefined ? \`, and against the rules in ${reviewer.repoFile} above.\` : ".")`.
  - The example and the shape line use `reviewer: reviewer.id` (`"code"` for the built-in) and finding ids `F1` stay.
- `CodeReviewerOptions`: add `reviewer?: PromptReviewer`. `runCodeReviewer` passes `opts.reviewer` (default `BUILTIN_CODE`) as the 6th argument; `kind` defaults to `opts.reviewer?.id ?? "code"`.
- **IMPORTS**: `{ BUILTIN_INSTRUCTIONS, BUILTIN_REVIEWERS } from "../review/reviewers.js"`, `{ repoText } from "../review/context.js"` (type import of `ReviewerContext` already exists).

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/tester.ts`

- `testerPrompt(ctx, round, reportPath, previous?, reviewer: PromptReviewer = BUILTIN_REVIEWERS[1]!)`:
  - Role lines from `reviewer.instructions` (empty → `BUILTIN_INSTRUCTIONS.tester`).
  - `const how = repoText(ctx, reviewer.repoFile)`; section title `` `## How to test this app (${reviewer.repoFile})` ``; bullets `` `- Follow ${reviewer.repoFile} above: boot the app …` `` / `` `- There is no ${reviewer.repoFile}: work out how to boot the app …` `` (rest of each line unchanged).
  - Everything else unchanged (plan, previous report, fixer summary, report shape with `reviewer: "tester"`).
- `LiveTesterOptions`: add `reviewer?: PromptReviewer`; `runLiveTester` passes it.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase.ts` (`reviewRound`)

- `buildReviewerContext({ ..., repoFiles: reviewers.map((r) => r.repoFile) })`.
- Round-0 log lines: for each reviewer whose `repoText(context, r.repoFile)` is undefined:
  - `code`: `no REVIEW.md at the repo root; the code reviewer applies general rules` — but with `r.repoFile` in place of `REVIEW.md`;
  - `tester`: `no TESTING.md at the repo root; the live tester works from the README and scripts` — with `r.repoFile`;
  - others: `` `no ${r.repoFile} at the repo root; ${r.name} works from its instructions` ``.
  (Built-ins: identical to today's lines.)
- In `runOne(reviewer)` for `type: "diff"`:
  - `let matched = matchFiles(context.changedFiles, reviewer.files)`; when `opts.reviewFiles` is set, also keep only files in `opts.reviewFiles`.
  - When `reviewer.files?.length` and `matched.length === 0` (and no valid report exists yet): write the report `{ round, reviewer: id, notes: [\`${stepName(reviewer)} not needed: no changed file matches its files\`], findings: [] }` exactly like the `CODE_REVIEW_NOT_NEEDED` branch (mkdir, write, log `${reviewStep(...)}: …`, `onReport`) and return it without running an agent.
  - When `reviewer.files?.length` and some match: `const diff = await diffOf(opts.integrationWorktree, opts.startingCommit, matched)` and pass `context: { ...context, diff }`.
  - Pass `reviewer` (the `PromptReviewer` fields) to `runCodeReviewer`; pass `reviewer` to `runLiveTester` for the tester.
- **GOTCHA**: the existing `opts.reviewFiles?.length === 0` shortcut (suite e2e) stays as is, before this filter.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.ts`

- `export const FAKE_PROMPTS_ENV = "GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_PROMPTS";` In `run(opts)`, after the log append: `const dir = process.env[FAKE_PROMPTS_ENV]; if (dir) { mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); writeFileSync(path.join(dir, \`${opts.role}-${opts.label.replace(/[^\w.-]+/g, "-")}.md\`), opts.prompt); }` (sync fs, so the file exists before the agent "runs"; a later attempt of the same label overwrites it).
- Add the env var to the doc list in `TESTING.md` ("Fake provider scripts", one line: "`GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_PROMPTS=<dir>` writes each agent prompt to `<dir>/<role>-<label>.md`").

### Tests

- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/context.test.ts`: add a case with `repoFiles: ["SECURITY_REVIEW.md", "REVIEW.md"]`, only `SECURITY_REVIEW.md` present (uncommitted) → `ctx.repoFiles` is `{ "SECURITY_REVIEW.md": "…" }`, no `reviewMd`. `diffOf` with one of two changed files → diff contains only that file.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/reviewer-prompt.test.ts` (new): default `codeReviewerPrompt(ctx, 0, "/r.json")` equals `codeReviewerPrompt(ctx, 0, "/r.json", undefined, [], BUILTIN_REVIEWERS[0])`; and with a security reviewer `{ id: "security", name: "Security", instructions: "Check auth.", repoFile: "SECURITY_REVIEW.md" }` and `ctx.repoFiles = { "SECURITY_REVIEW.md": "Public: /health", "REVIEW.md": "No console.log" }`: starts with `Check auth.`, contains `## Review rules (SECURITY_REVIEW.md)` and `Public: /health`, does NOT contain `No console.log` nor `You are the code reviewer`, contains `` `reviewer` "security" ``.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase-reviewers.test.ts` (exists from the earlier slice; add cases), with `runReview(script, { reviewers })`:
  - write `SECURITY_REVIEW.md` ("SEC-MARKER") and `REVIEW.md` ("REVIEW-MARKER") uncommitted at the repo root: the `security-r0` prompt contains `SEC-MARKER` and not `REVIEW-MARKER`; the `code-r0` prompt contains `REVIEW-MARKER` and not `SEC-MARKER`; the tester prompt contains neither.
  - without `SECURITY_REVIEW.md`: log line `no SECURITY_REVIEW.md at the repo root; Security works from its instructions`, and the security reviewer still ran.
  - `files: ["nothing/**"]` → `security.json` has a `not needed` note and there is no `reviewer:security-r0` call; `files: ["1.txt"]` → its prompt's diff contains `1.txt` and not `2.txt` (the diamond fixture commits `1.txt`…`4.txt`).
  - a tester with `instructions: "Only check the API."` and `repoFile: "QA.md"` (present) → tester prompt starts with `Only check the API.` and contains `## How to test this app (QA.md)`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.test.ts` (or the closest existing fake-provider test): with `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_PROMPTS` set, a run writes `reviewer-code-r0.md` holding the prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Built-in reviewers: prompts byte-identical to today (existing snapshot/prompt tests pass unchanged).
- [ ] A `security` reviewer with `repoFile: SECURITY_REVIEW.md` gets that file's text when it exists at the repo root (even uncommitted), under `## Review rules (SECURITY_REVIEW.md)`, and never `REVIEW.md`; the code reviewer never gets `SECURITY_REVIEW.md`.
- [ ] Without the file, the run logs `no SECURITY_REVIEW.md at the repo root` and the reviewer still runs.
- [ ] `instructions` replace the role text for diff reviewers and the tester; the frame (report path, shape, finding rules, previous report) is unchanged.
- [ ] `files` limits the diff; no match → "not needed" report, no agent run.
- [ ] `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_PROMPTS=<dir>` writes `<role>-<label>.md` prompts.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- context reviewer tester phase fake
npm test
```
